description: Refine the orch-agent-allowlist PreToolUse hook to capability-based policy gated by CAM_SESSION scope, plus implementer issue/PRD anchoring.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Command hooks run in the current directory with Claude Code's environment, so CAM_SESSION injected on the tmux new-session is visible to the hook subprocess. DENY contract = exit 0 + JSON stdout {hookSpecificOutput:{permissionDecision:'deny'}}; the spawned subagent type lives in tool_input.subagent_type, while top-level agent_type is the caller identity. The CAM-91 three-path read keeps subagent_type primary and falls through to the caller (subagent-orchestrator, not in the read-only set) on misread, so it errs to DENY, never a false ALLOW.

userStories.title: Rewrite runtime hook to capability policy gated by CAM_SESSION
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need the runtime allowlist hook to allow read-only subagents while denying code-writers only inside cam-managed sessions, so that the orchestrator can spawn Explore/Plan helpers but interactive dev sessions stay unrestricted.
acceptanceCriteria: When CAM_SESSION is unset, the hook exits 0 with empty stdout (allow) for any subagent type including general-purpose and absent type. [oracle: bun test]
When CAM_SESSION is set, subagent types {Explore, Plan, claude-code-guide, subagent-planner, subagent-auditor, subagent-reviewer} yield ALLOW (exit 0, empty stdout). [oracle: bun test]
When CAM_SESSION is set, subagent types {general-purpose, claude, fork, subagent-implementer} yield DENY (exit 0, JSON stdout with permissionDecision 'deny'). [oracle: bun test]
When CAM_SESSION is set, an absent/empty subagent type and an unknown type (e.g. 'foobar') both yield DENY. [oracle: bun test]

The hook header-comment and permissionDecisionReason describe the capability+scope model (no longer a fixed name allowlist of {subagent-planner, subagent-auditor}). [oracle: grep -q -i 'capability' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/.claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh]
The hook header-comment and reason reference the CAM_SESSION scope gate. [oracle: grep -q 'CAM_SESSION' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/.claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh]

The three-path subagent_type extraction (.tool_input.subagent_type // .tool_input.agent_type // .agent_type) is unchanged. [oracle: grep -q 'tool_input.subagent_type // .tool_input.agent_type // .agent_type' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/.claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh]

runHook accepts an explicit env arg; an unscoped case (CAM_SESSION absent from the passed env) ALLOWs general-purpose EVEN WHEN the parent process env has CAM_SESSION set, and a scoped case (CAM_SESSION present in the passed env) applies the capability policy, both deterministic regardless of ambient CAM_SESSION. [oracle: bun test]

The test passes an explicit env object to Bun.spawn that controls CAM_SESSION (not inheriting ambient env). [oracle: grep -Eq 'env:' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts]
Existing test cases whose semantics changed (e.g. Explore previously expected deny) are corrected in place, not duplicated, and the full new matrix is covered. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, test/orch-agent-allowlist.test.ts. The hook is read at runtime from .claude/ by Claude Code; NO binary rebuild needed for it to take effect this session (rebuild only matters for downstream cam init, handled in US-002). Gate CAM_SESSION at the top: `if [ -z "${CAM_SESSION:-}" ]; then exit 0; fi` BEFORE the payload read. Replace the name `case` with capability policy: ALLOW set {Explore, Plan, claude-code-guide, subagent-planner, subagent-auditor, subagent-reviewer}, everything else (incl. absent/unknown) = DENY (default-deny preserved WITHIN scope). Security direction preserved: misread falls through to caller identity subagent-orchestrator (not in ALLOW set) -> DENY, never false allow. CRITICAL test fix (CAM-59/60 green-local!=green-CI class): runHook today does NOT pass env to Bun.spawn so it inherits ambient CAM_SESSION (set locally, unset on CI). runHook MUST accept an explicit env override and pass `env:` to Bun.spawn; add a case that proves the UNSCOPED path (env built WITHOUT CAM_SESSION) ALLOWs general-purpose EVEN WHEN the parent process has CAM_SESSION set — locking that the test does not depend on inherited ambient CAM_SESSION. Project lesson (CLAUDE.md): 'comment does not prove behavior' — update the header-comment WITH the logic or it goes stale. Do NOT touch the three-path extraction logic. Skill: none beyond bash + bun:test.

userStories.title: Operator dogfood: live end-to-end hook behavior
userStories.description: As the operator, I need to observe real subagent spawns in a live cam session, so that the capability policy and scope gate behave as designed against actual Claude Code payloads.
acceptanceCriteria: In an active cam session (CAM_SESSION set), the orchestrator spawning an Explore subagent is ALLOWED (previously denied). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
In the same session, spawning general-purpose remains DENIED. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
A non-cam interactive claude session (CAM_SESSION unset) is unaffected: all spawns allowed. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: requires: 'operator' (literal string) — the supervisor source (src/supervisor/loop.ts:518 and src/commands/sidecar.ts:211) only skips a story when requires === 'operator'; any other value (e.g. a story id) makes the supervisor autonomously dispatch this operator-only dogfood, which is wrong. The implementer must exit with BLOCKED_OPERATOR_REQUIRED. Needs observation of real subagent spawns in a live cam session, which the implementer cannot perform. The hook is runtime-read from .claude/ so US-001 takes effect this session without rebuild; the template/embed path (US-002/US-004) only matters for downstream cam init. Lesson (project): fakes lie — operator smoke caught criticals that green tests missed (CAM-55), hence this live check.
